newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down on weak Q3 company results.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down on weak Q3 company results.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down on Monday on weak volume because investors were disappointed with third quarter company results, brokers said.

Following a slew of weak company results at the end of last week, Alejandro Arrieta of local brokerage Divisas y Valores said: "We could not have expected the session to be different after the companies' third quarter results."

Brokers said the market was likely to stay in its slump. The government will publish September's gross domestic product figure on Tuesday, which will probably confirm fears the country's economy will underperform expectations, they added.
Accounting for 51 percent of the market's volume, benchmark Telefonica del Peru was the most heavily traded stock as it fell 1.28 percent to 5.39 soles.
Among other leaders, Credicorp Ltd. fell 4.41 percent to $16.92 in ten percent of total volume. Tin-miner Minsur fell 3.67 percent to 22.30 soles in seven percent percent of the day's volume.
Monday, the General Index .IGRA fell 1.12 percent to 1,483.55 points and the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL fell 1.70 percent to 2,050.68 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 1,698 trades, 45 stocks fell, 32 were stable and 10 rose in volume of 31.5 million ($12.2 million).
According to latest government figures, the Peruvian economy grew 2.0 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared with 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.
The government is predicting annual growth of between three and four percent in 1996, down from initial projections of between five and six percent due to an economic slowdown earlier in the year.

While investors were aware this year's slower economic growth would have an effect on financial results they expected some companies to outperform the general economy. But, in the end, blue-chip stocks across the board refelected the general slowdown, brokers said.
